result.topic_en: Latin draft passage outlining how to solve the general problem of the Paris prize question (which coefficient functions b and quantity k allow u to be independent of one variable, and when the quadratic differential form can be transformed into a constant-coefficient form, by Gauss's method from the theory of curved surfaces), followed by notation for the case where u does not depend on γ.
result.transcription:
Transformatio igitur [-reduci-] expressionis

[-reducitur-].

Solutio igitur quaestionis nostrae generalis eo redit, ut primo quaeratur -

[-Iam-]
[-Quae-] {+Quae+} quum ita sint, problema nostrum generale hoc modo solvere possumus

{+ut primum quaeramus+} [-primum-] quales esse debeant functiones $b_{\iota\iota'}$ {+et $k$+} quantitatum $s_1, s_2, s_3$, ut $u$ [-un posset fun-] ab una harum quantitatum [-independens-] non dependere possit; [-Deinde, ut inveniatur, an hoc-] tum expressionis $\Sigma\, b_{\iota\iota'}\, ds_\iota\, ds_{\iota'}$ formari potest
Tum ut [-inveniatur, an hoc pro-] datis valoribus {+quantitatum+} [-quarum-] $a_{\iota\iota'}$ et quantitatis $k$ inveniamus, [-quibusnam-] {+num+} an $u$ functio [-ipsius-] temporis et duarum tantum variabilium fieri possit et quibusnam in casibus [-quaerendum-] est, an {+expressio+} $\Sigma\, b_{\iota\iota'}\, ds_\iota\, ds_{\iota'}$ in formam datam $\Sigma\, \alpha_{\iota\iota'}\, dx_\iota\, dx_{\iota'}$ transformari possit {+et haec+} [-Quam-] [-quidem-] quaestionem ipsa videbimus eadem {+fere+} methodo tractari posse, qua [-Ill-] Gaussius [-in-] in theoria superficierum curvarum usus est.

Ut denotationem {+simpliciorem+} {+expeditiorem+} commodiorem reddamus, [-designemus-] [-variabiles pro-] {+quantitates+} $s_1, s_2, s_3$ per $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ designemus et formam per

$\begin{pmatrix} a, & b, & c \\ a', & b', & c' \end{pmatrix}$.

[-Ubi-] {+Si+} $u$ a $\gamma$ [-non-] pendet, aequatio differentialis erit formae
$a\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\alpha^2} + [-2c'-] \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta} + b\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\beta^2} + s\frac{\partial u}{\partial\alpha} + t\frac{\partial u}{\partial\beta} = k\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$
{+posito+} [-denotando-] $\frac{\partial a}{\partial\alpha} + \frac{\partial c'}{\partial\beta} + \frac{\partial b'}{\partial\gamma} = s$ \quad $\frac{\partial b}{\partial\beta} + \frac{\partial c'}{\partial\alpha} + \frac{\partial a'}{\partial\gamma} = t$


[-Aequatio igitur ex qua-] [-ut-]

I

[-Cas.-]


II.

methods.what: Reduce question of transformability of quadratic differential form to constant-coefficient form by Gauss's method for curved surfaces
methods.quote: an {+expressio+} $\Sigma\, b_{\iota\iota'}\, ds_\iota\, ds_{\iota'}$ in formam datam $\Sigma\, \alpha_{\iota\iota'}\, dx_\iota\, dx_{\iota'}$ transformari possit

methods.what: Notation for symmetric coefficient form in variables α, β, γ
methods.quote: $\begin{pmatrix} a, & b, & c \\ a', & b', & c' \end{pmatrix}$

methods.what: Heat equation in two variables when u independent of γ, with first-order coefficients s, t defined as divergence-type sums
methods.quote: $a\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\alpha^2} + [-2c'-] \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta} + b\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\beta^2} + s\frac{\partial u}{\partial\alpha} + t\frac{\partial u}{\partial\beta} = k\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$

items.english: that we first seek what the functions b_{ιι'} and k of the quantities s1, s2, s3 must be so that u can fail to depend on one of these quantities

items.english: for given values of the quantities a_{ιι'} and the quantity k, we find whether u can be a function of time and only two variables

items.english: we shall see that this question can be treated by almost the same method that Gauss used in the theory of curved surfaces
